vulns.description: Certifi versions before 2026.10.18 include the `emSign ECC Root CA - G3` root certificate in their bundled CA store. Eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates that chain to this root have compromised private keys and the CA has revoked them.   An attacker with one of the compromised keys can issue valid-looking certificates for any hostname. If the attacker is also on-path, they can intercept or modify TLS traffic from clients that trust the certifi bundle. Examples include `requests`, `urllib3` and `pip`, and the Python.org macOS installer.  Certifi 2026.10.18 removed all emSign roots from the bundle. Certifi 2026.10.19 restored the emSign roots that are not affected. Upgrade to 2026.10.19 or later, and rebuild container images that vendor certifi.

### Summary In affected versions, a Streamable HTTP server in stateful mode (the default) never reclaimed session state:  - sessions did not expire; - a client `DELETE` ended the session but left its entry registered; - a session whose first request was refused stayed registered with a running task.  Each session also kept its parsed `initialize` parameters, and the number of sessions was unlimited. A client that could reach the endpoint could grow server memory without bound using ordinary short requests; only a restart reclaimed it.  ### Am I affected? Yes, if you serve MCP over Streamable HTTP in stateful mode and clients you do not fully trust can reach the endpoint. Stateful mode is the default for:  - `FastMCP` (1.x) - `MCPServer` and `Server.streamable_http_app()` (2.x) - `StreamableHTTPSessionManager`  Affected versions: 1.8.0 through 1.29.1, and 2.0.0 through 2.1.1.  Not affected:  - servers on 1.12.0 or later passing `stateless_http=True` (no sessions are kept) - servers using only the stdio or SSE transports  Authentication limits who can open sessions, not how many a token holder can open.  ### Fix Upgrade to `mcp` 1.30.0 (1.x) or 2.2.0 (2.x) or later. In those versions:  - a session with no request in flight for `session_idle_timeout` seconds (default 1800) is closed and its ID then answers `404`; open streams and in-progress requests keep it alive; - at most `max_sessions` sessions exist at once (default 10000); a request that would open another is answered `503`; - a session is discarded as soon as it ends, whether by `DELETE`, expiry, or a refused opening request.  Both settings are keyword arguments on `FastMCP(...)` (1.x), `MCPServer.run()` / `streamable_http_app()` (2.x) and `StreamableHTTPSessionManager`; `None` disables them.  This bounds retention rather than eliminating it: a live session still holds its `initialize` parameters (up to roughly twice the 4 MiB body limit), and an `initialize` with invalid parameters still opens a session that expires like any other. On a small host, lower `session_idle_timeout`, `max_sessions` and `max_request_body_size` to fit.  If you cannot upgrade yet, pass `stateless_http=True` (1.12.0 or later) where you need no per-session state, or restrict who can reach the endpoint.
